title: Crescent Ventures partner outreach scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad for Crescent Ventures (CV) — goal: pilot Redwood Inference for their internal customer insights tooling and offer a co-marketing case study if pilot hits SLAs.

Account snapshot
- Company: Crescent Ventures (mid-stage VC-backed retail analytics startup)
- HQ: Chicago + small R&D team in Austin
- Size: ~180 employees, Product + Eng ~60, Sales ~25
- Estimated ARR: $10–15M (self-serve + a few enterprise deals)
- Tech stack: Python backend, Kubernetes on AWS, Databricks + Snowflake for data; currently using OpenAI for prototypes (chat + embeddings)
- Current inference pain: token costs, unpredictable latency during batch scoring, difficulty shipping retraining/rollout workflows for model variants

Why Crescent could be a fit
- They have a clear ML infra use case (embedding-based search + customer insights) where we can show predictable per-token unit cost + average 30–50% cost reduction with batching + caching.
- Regulatory footprint is light but they care about data handling and private deployments for some larger retailer customers — good upsell path from hosted API -> Dedicated -> Private.
- They publish thought leadership (blog + webinars) and would likely co-market a pilot success story.

Key contacts (to verify via LinkedIn)
- Primary: Priya Malhotra — Head of Data Products (likes to talk scale and deployment reliability)
- Secondary: Jonah Park — Staff ML Engineer (owns features + infra decisions)
- Exec sponsor: Marcus Bell — VP Product (interested in cost/perf tradeoffs if it impacts margins)
- Procurement: TBA (likely appears late-stage)

Signal to call out in outreach
- They pay for cloud GPU inference indirectly via ad-hoc infra -> potential savings + predictable SLOs are compelling.
- Example problem: nightly batch embedding refresh of 40M rows causing throttling and higher egress/costs.
- Competitor signals: using just-in-time OpenAI + ad-hoc caching libs (no dedicated serving runtime)

Value props to highlight (short bullets for email / call)
- Predictable per-token costs + billing transparency (token-level breakdowns per route)
- 30–50% token cost reduction for typical embedding/score workloads via batching & caching recommendations
- Dedicated pools for predictable throughput and SLAs (good for retailer customers asking for data isolation)
- Simple API parity so product teams can prototype on hosted and later move to Dedicated/Private without rewrite

Outbound sequence (2-week cadence, flexible)
1) Email 1 (intro + one-liner value + ask for 20m demo)
2) LinkedIn connection + short note referencing email
3) Phone warm follow (if number available) / Calendly link in email 2 with 2 suggested times
4) Targeted follow up sharing a 1-page pilot outline + high level pricing
5) Attempt to engage via mutuals (VC contact or public blog author)

Email draft — subject ideas
- "Reduce embedding costs and stabilize inference for Crescent Ventures"
- "Quick pilot to cut inference cost variability — 20m?"

Email draft v1 (short, personalized)
Hi Priya —

I’m Ethan from Redwood Inference. We help engineering teams reduce per-token inference cost while keeping latency predictable and shipping model rollouts safely. I noticed Crescent Ventures runs nightly embedding refreshes and has begun prototyping with OpenAI — two areas where our customers often see immediate wins.

A 20m pilot can show: a) predictable per-token cost estimates for your workload, b) batching/caching config that often trims costs 30%+, and c) a deployment plan that keeps your product teams on the same API as you scale to dedicated capacity.

Are you open to a quick call next week? Happy to share a one-page pilot plan beforehand.

Best,
Ethan

Call script (3-min opener)
- Intro / one-line value
- Quick check: confirm who owns embedding pipeline and pain points (latency, cost, reliability)
- Offer quick metric: “Customers with similar setups cut embedding costs by ~30% in early tuning”
- Close: request 20–30m workshop with Jonah + one engineer to bring logs/metrics

Objection handling (short snippets)
- "We already use OpenAI / not interested": "Totally — many teams prototype on OpenAI. Redwood is designed so you can keep your dev experience but reduce variability and cost at scale; pilot can be low-commitment and show concrete numbers on your own traffic."
- "Procurement/budget concerns": "Pilot is time-limited and focused on measurable cost/latency impact. If the economics look compelling we can discuss reserved capacity options later; if not, you keep the findings."
- "We're building infra in-house": "Totally understand. A quick pilot can act as a benchmark for your in-house work — if we don’t win on economics/latency, you gain a concrete performance baseline to improve against."

Pilot proposal (one-paragraph summary for follow-up email)
- Duration: 4 weeks (2 weeks ingestion + tuning, 2 weeks validation)
- Scope: embeddings pipeline + scoring endpoint for web product; measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and per-token cost; run A/B vs current pipeline on 10–20% traffic or on nightly batch sample
- Success criteria: >=25% cost reduction OR p95 latency improvement of at least 20% while keeping quality parity
- Deliverable: configuration recommendations, dashboard access, and a short case study (if customer agrees)

Notes / research TODOs
- Verify headcount numbers on LinkedIn (Priya, Jonah, Marcus).
- Check company blog for recent customer announcements (retailer references).
- Find any mentions of batch-size / nightly refresh cadence (GitHub or engineering blog posts).
- Ask Solutions Eng to prepare a trimmed demo that shows our embedding caching + cost dashboard for a 40M-row scenario.

Next steps (this doc)
- Finalize email and run by Priya Chen for tone + legal checks (Maya to review) — target send: Mon 3/16
- Book demo slot with Solutions Eng (Priya N.) to build sample dataset run: requested by 3/19
- Create pilot one-pager and attach to follow-up email

Random scratch ideas / phrases to test in outreach
- "pilot to make inference costs predictable — not just lower"
- "no code rewrites for product teams — same API from prototype to dedicated"
- "show me the money: cost dashboard for your exact workloads"

End of scratchpad. Keep rough. Update after first call.
